name: Pet bowl size and height guidance

rules.rule: Rim from elbow height down to 7.5 cm (3 in) below it
rules.evidence: rule of thumb from pet-product guides; no veterinary guideline

rules.rule: Floor level or the usual rim height: the studies disagree. Dogs with megaesophagus are fed from a raised position on purpose (front legs higher than back legs, upright at least 10 to 15 minutes after meals)
rules.evidence: cohort study, more than 1,600 dogs: raised bowls linked to about 20% (large) and 52% (giant) of GDV cases; internet survey, 1,114 GDV cases: no clear effect of bowl height, no numbers published

rules.rule: Dish at least as wide as the whisker span
rules.evidence: 38-cat study: no difference in time eating, food dropped or food eaten; 63% of owners said their cat preferred the wide dish

rules.rule: At least 1.5 x the meal volume, 2 x for a slow feeder; 1 US cup = 236.6 ml
A slow feeder lengthens the meal
rules.evidence: 10-dog study showed slower eating; no trial shows bloat prevention

rules.rule: Size by elbow height, not weight
Narrower opening or a tilted bowl
RER = 70 x kg^0.75 kcal/day; MER = RER x factor (dog: neutered 1.6, intact 1.8, inactive 1.2-1.4, growth 2-3; cat: neutered 1.2, intact 1.4, inactive 1.0, growth 2-3); cups = MER / kcal per cup
rules.evidence: Pet Nutrition Alliance table; estimates only, pets can vary by as much as 50%, adjust to body condition

rules.rule: Choose a food labelled complete and balanced for the life stage; for puppies that will be large dogs, the label should include growth of large size dogs
rules.evidence: label rule; large-breed puppies need tighter calcium limits
